description: A contract that exercises every feature of the manifest format the TypeScript emitter has to answer for.

Nobody would write this contract: it is not a design, it is a checklist. Every scalar keyword appears, every one of the three field states appears, both taggings appear, a variant travels under a wire spelling that is not its name, a field's keys are written beside its siblings, a shape is imported from another file, and every one of those carries the prose the format requires — which is what the golden files assert becomes a doc comment.
The event envelope and the direction it travelled, shared with every other contract that carries events. Restating them here would be a second definition with nothing saying the two are the same.

types.name: Scalars
description: Every scalar keyword the format has, once each, plus the two ways a list is written.
This shape exists so that a change to the scalar table shows up as a diff in a golden file rather than as a surprise in somebody's browser.

fields.name: text
description: UTF-8 text.

fields.name: flag
description: True or false.

fields.name: small_signed
description: A signed 32-bit integer. Inside a double's exact range by construction.

fields.name: small_unsigned
description: An unsigned 32-bit integer.

fields.name: safe_signed
description: A signed integer the contract promises is inside the range a double holds exactly.

fields.name: safe_unsigned
description: The unsigned half of the same promise.

fields.name: wide_signed
description: A signed integer that may exceed the safe range. Saying so is the warning the keyword exists to give: a target whose only number is a double must carry this as an arbitrary-precision value or lose it.

fields.name: wide_unsigned
description: The unsigned half of the same warning.

fields.name: fraction
description: A double.

fields.name: where_it_runs
description: A filesystem path, as a string. Resolved on the producer's machine, which is the fact the keyword carries and the type does not.

fields.name: passthrough
description: Arbitrary JSON, forwarded without being interpreted.

fields.name: lines
description: A list of a scalar.

fields.name: directions
description: A list of an imported named type.

types.name: Filter
description: A predicate whose every field is null rather than absent, because that is the form this wire already had before it was written down.

fields.name: since_ms
description: Exclusive lower bound, or null for the start of the log.

fields.name: direction
description: Keep only this direction, or null to keep both.

types.name: States
description: One field in each of the four states a field can be in.

Required, absent-able, null-able and defaulted are four different things on the wire, and the whole reason the format spends three keys on them is that a decoder in another language has to be told which. This is where the emitter proves it passes all four through.

fields.name: required_text
description: Always written, and an object without it is malformed.

fields.name: optional_text
description: May be absent, and absence means nothing was said. A writer omits the key rather than writing null.

fields.name: nullable_text
description: Always written, and null when there is nothing to say.

fields.name: include_history
description: Whether to merge ended sessions into the answer.

Absent means true, which is what a person looking at a list wants. A reader who assumed false would quietly get a different answer than the contract gives, which is why the value is in the manifest rather than in each implementation.

fields.name: page_size
description: How many rows at most. Absent means a page a human can read.

fields.name: label
description: What to call this in a listing.

fields.name: backend
description: Which backend to assume. The default is written as the wire spelling and not as the variant name, because the wire is what a default is a value of.

fields.name: filter
description: The row predicate. Absent means the filter that selects everything.

types.name: Request
description: What a caller sends, whose own keys are the ones on the wire.

fields.name: subject
description: What the request is about.

fields.name: attempts
description: How many times the caller has tried.

types.name: Trace
description: Where a request came from, carried alongside it rather than inside it.

fields.name: origin
description: Who asked.

types.name: StartArgs
description: The caller's own request, plus what this producer needs on top of it.
The request is carried whole and its keys are the ones on the wire. Re-spelling them here would be a second definition of a shape the caller already sends.

fields.name: request
description: The caller's request. Not a key: its own keys are written here.

fields.name: max_event_ts
description: The resume seed, when the caller has one.

types.name: Envelope
description: A shape whose every field is flattened, so there is no object half of its own at all.

fields.name: request
description: The request, whole.

fields.name: trace
description: Where it came from, whole.

types.name: Ack
description: An answer with nothing in it. A shape with no keys is not the same as a shape that could have any, which is what the generated type has to say.

types.name: Backend
description: Which backend a session runs against.

variants.name: claude_code
description: Two words on the wire, hyphenated. A live TypeScript consumer reads this exact spelling, so it is the contract and not a rendering choice.

variants.name: codex
description: One word, so the name and the wire value are the same and only one of them is written.

types.name: Event
description: One thing that happened.

fields.name: meta
description: When it happened and which way it went. An imported shape, used as a field's type.

fields.name: line
description: The raw line that crossed.

types.name: Item
description: One item on the watch stream, internally tagged.
Internal tagging is the form to prefer for a new contract: a reader dispatches on one key without knowing the arm names in advance, which is exactly what a TypeScript discriminated union narrows on.

variants.name: event
description: One event, carried whole. Its keys sit beside the discriminator, so a consumer that already holds one puts it on the stream and takes it off again rather than taking it apart and rebuilding it.

variants.name: gap
description: Events this reader will never receive, reported rather than skipped.

fields.name: lost
description: How many, as an upper bound. Wide because a gap in a long-running stream has no small bound.

fields.name: note
description: Why, when the producer knows.

variants.name: done
description: The stream has nothing further. An arm with no payload and no fields at all, travelling under a wire spelling that is not its name.

types.name: Choice
description: Which backends a read keeps, externally tagged.
Externally tagged because one arm carries a list, and there is nowhere inside a JSON array to put a discriminator key. That case is the entire reason the format has two taggings.

variants.name: only
description: Keep rows whose backend is in the set. An empty set keeps nothing.

variants.name: except
description: Drop rows whose backend is in the set. An empty set drops nothing.

variants.name: named
description: Keep rows matching a name, with the criteria spelled out as this arm's own keys rather than as a shape.

fields.name: prefix
description: The prefix to match.

fields.name: case_sensitive
description: Whether case matters. Absent means it does not.

variants.name: everything
description: Keep every row. An externally tagged arm with neither a payload nor fields is a bare string on the wire, not an object with a null value.

errors.name: demo_every_refused
description: The producer declined. Carries an empty shape, which is enough to exercise an error with typed data.

ops.name: demo.every.list
description: Every matching event.

ops.name: demo.every.latest
description: The newest matching event, or nothing at all when there is none. Not an absent result: this op answers, and sometimes the answer is that there is none.

ops.name: demo.every.start
description: Start a session and answer that it started.

ops.name: demo.every.watch
description: The session's items, as they happen.
